connector.why: Counts all 175 of Abraham's years, childhood before he knew his Creator included, through לך טל ילדותך (BR 39:8) and the same Lech Lecha 7: the very mechanism of 'their years are whole' here.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 15:2
connector.why: התהלך לפני והיה תמים reached through the covenant of circumcision, with טל ילדותך covering Abraham's youth; the theme is temimus as knowing all is from God, not the wholeness of his years.
Abraham's 48 years before knowing God 'evaporate like dew' (BR 39) so he becomes אזרח; same Midrash and the redemption of the early years, but the point is Abraham being called Israel.
Shares התהלך לפני and BR 14:6 only in passing; the passage is about Torah against imagination and levels of hishtadlus.

Abraham's youth 'dear as dew' (BR 39) under the rule ברישא חשוכא והדר נהורא: the same pairing of טל ילדותך with light out of darkness that this maamar makes, applied to the Avodah Zarah tractate and אזרחי.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8:4
connector.why: Cites טל ילדותך in one clause about Abraham becoming אזרח; the passage is about three kinds of wisdom (Adam, Noah, Abraham).
Through טל ילדותך and מרחם משחר Abraham, first of converts, is revealed as holy from the womb, so that 'the earlier' is changed too: the redemption of the pre-knowledge years, here for teshuvah.
Reads טל ילדותך (via Shocher Tov) as Abraham's youthful zeal for mitzvos; a different idea from the counting of childhood years.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:30
connector.why: Same two sources (אשה כמאן דמהילא, ואשה בכל אלה לא מצאתי) but used to say a woman lacks wisdom; the opposite of Sarah's unique wholeness here.
Reads שני חיי שרה and BR 58 (ימי תמימים) as her days being full and not cut short at the Akeidah; same verse and Midrash, different sense of 'whole years'.
After Isaac's birth Abraham became אזרח and 'repaired his childhood as if born in holiness' (BR 39:8, טל ילדותך): the redemption of the early years.
Shares only 'Bereshit Rabbah 39' (a different piece, the weeders in the Land); about Shabbat and shemittah.
Tzaddikim go מחיל אל חיל in the next world as in this one (Berachos 64a): the premise of the maamar's last section, that a scholar's life keeps growing after death.
Same Gemara and Rashi (מישיבה לישיבה) applied to weekdays and Shabbat, chassan and kallah; no link to the years of the righteous.
Quotes 'tzaddikim have no rest' to contrast Jacob's rest with Esau's; a different theme.

candidates.why: Quotes the Midrash and asks the same questions (why עגלתא, what is the dearness in both worlds), but the passage itself turns to burial, Machpelah and intellect versus Torah; the answer comes in 28:5.

כהדא עגלתא as every part of a life joined to its inner point, so that 'their years are whole' and each year is bound to the next; Sarah was never separated from the root of life for a moment. The same reading of the circle-calf as the equality and wholeness of all the tzaddik's years, from the Izhbitz circle's contemporary.

Uses ימי תמימים to show Sarah lived her full allotted span and her death was not caused by the Akeidah; a different sense of 'whole years' (not cut short), as in Poked Akarim, not the counting of every year.
Halachic pilpul (read through Chayei Sara 8-14): whether Sarah was punished for חמסי עליך and whether a woman may judge; the calf is a blemished-but-'whole' animal. Not Rav Tzadok's idea.

Explains the doubled שני חיי שרה as a second, lasting dimension of her years (the sanctified body), which is why they are dear in this world and the next: the same exegetical problem (the repetition = dearness in the World to Come), with a different answer.

found.why: Asks why the Midrash adds 'whole in her deeds' and the calf image for Sarah and not Abraham, and answers that Abraham's wholeness came from intellect while Sarah's came from the body and deeds; a parallel to Rav Tzadok's question why this is hinted in Sarah and not in Abraham.
Abraham repaired Adam's sin and Sarah repaired Eve's; the same pairing on which the maamar builds Sarah's uniqueness ('a woman among all these I have not found').

Maharal on 'Torah scholars have no rest... in the World to Come': Torah understanding has no completion, so the scholar keeps going מחיל אל חיל even there. This is Rav Tzadok's premise that life is added to scholars after death.
The tzaddik goes from level to level without end, never resting at any level of understanding, in this world or the next (Berachos 64a); the same reading of the Gemara that Rav Tzadok needs.

footnotes.text:
**Sefat Emet, Bereishis, Chayei Sarah 2 (5632)** (Chassidus) — Reads כהדא עגלתא תמימתא as a life whose every part is joined to its inner point, so the tzaddik's years are bound to one another and none falls outside the whole; Sarah was never separated from the root of life even for a moment. This parallels the Izhbitzer's circle in which every point is equal, which Rav Tzadok applies to all of Sarah's years.
וכמו כן שנותיהם תמימים כי גם ימי השנה יש להם דביקות ושייכות

**Midbar Shur 28:5** (Machshava) — Rav Kook also takes up the repeated שני חיי שרה. For him the repetition marks years that stand and endure through the sanctity of the body, which is why the lives of the righteous are dear in this world and in the next. Rav Tzadok works from the same repetition but explains it by a woman's life staying at its number.
וכפל שני חיי שרה שהם שנים עומדות וקיימות מפני קדושת הגוף הקיימת

**Shem MiShmuel, Chayei Sarah 11:4** (Chassidus) — Asks why the Midrash adds 'whole in her deeds' and the unblemished calf for Sarah and not for Abraham. He answers that Abraham's wholeness came from the intellect and Sarah's from the heart, the body and deeds. Rav Tzadok asks the same question (why Sarah and not Abraham) but answers it through her repair of Eve.
וע"כ לא אמרו זה באברהם, שתמימות אברהם בכולל הראש והלב באו מפאת השכל

**Megalleh Amukkot, Va'eschanan, ofan 235** (Kabbalah) — Abraham repaired Adam's sin of thought and Sarah repaired Eve's sin of deed, and Isaac completed both. This is the same pairing (Abraham for Adam, Sarah for Eve) on which Rav Tzadok bases Sarah's uniqueness among women.
בא אברהם ותיקן חטא של אדם במחשבה, ושרה תקנה מעשה של חוה

**Maharal, Nesivos Olam, Nesiv HaTorah 9** (Machshava) — Explains 'Torah scholars have no rest' as meaning that Torah understanding never reaches completion, so the scholar keeps advancing מחיל אל חיל even in the World to Come. This is Rav Tzadok's premise that scholars' lives keep growing after death and so cannot be described as 'kept at their number'.
וגם בעולם הבא אין מנוחה לתלמידי חכמים, כאשר כל השגה אין בה השלמה

**Me'or Einayim, Hosafos 15** (Chassidus) — Reads the same Gemara as the tzaddik going from level to level without end, never resting at one level of understanding, in this world or the next. The same reading of 'no rest' as endless growth underlies Rav Tzadok's contrast between the righteous men and Sarah.
שהצדיק הולך תמיד ממדריגה למדריגה עד אין סוף ואין תכלית
